<br>

Let $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be the parameters of our neural network. 

We have a differentiable loss function $\mathcal{L}: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ that tells us how good our model performs. We aim to successively update $\theta^{(0)} \to \theta^{(0)} \to \dots$ such that it minimizes $\mathcal{L}(\theta)$.

Let $\Delta \theta$ denote such an update to our parameters. Each update is as follows
$$
\theta^{(t+1)} \gets \theta^{(t)} + \Delta \theta^{(t)}.
$$

Now, how to find a good update $\Delta \theta$ given our current parameters and gradients only ?
